newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault in talks on dealer reorganisation.
newsitem.headline: Renault in talks on dealer reorganisation.

text.p: French carmaker Renault opened talks with its trade unions on Tuesday on reorganising its money-losing dealer network, company and union officials said.

The talks are part of Renault's efforts to improve its performance after reporting a 5.25 billion French franc ($923.1 million) loss for 1996. The group set a target of 20 billion francs in savings between now and the year 2000 at a weekend meeting of managers.
Chairman Louis Schweitzer said last week that Renault was considering absorbing its wholly owned dealers, who account for around a third of sales, into a subsidiary with a profit centre.
Currently 24 Renault dealers have subsidiary status and 53 are owned by the group. The independent dealers, who account for two-thirds of sales, would not be touched by the reorganisation.
"We began talks on the subject today," a Renault spokeswoman said. They were expected to last "several days, weeks," she said.

The Socialist-led CFDT union issued a statement on Tuesday asking for an extraordinary staff works meeting to discuss the issue. It said it opposed any plan by management to impose a decision to transform its dealers into a subsidiary.

Schweitzer had said one of the advantages of such a move would be that it would allow for a change in the status of some dealer employees, who are currently covered by the metallurgical workers' convention.
It has lost 550 million francs since 1992. Schweitzer said last week that its performance was worse than that of the group subsidiaries.
